units.function: Creates a bearer bootstrap_ceo human invitation directly in Paperclip's database for authenticated deployments. It loads config/env, resolves database and public base URLs, refuses when an instance admin exists unless --force, revokes unaccepted/unexpired bootstrap invites, inserts a hashed random-token invite, prints its URL/expiry and closes the database client.
units.dependencyDirection: Privileged CLI command -> config/env and deployment bind inference -> @paperclipai/db schema/client and Drizzle -> invites/instanceUserRoles tables. It bypasses the server application/authz/audit layer and directly mutates identity authority state; URL composition is local config/environment logic rather than a canonical IdentityPort origin contract.
units.keyDataModels: instance_admin role; invite{inviteType=bootstrap_ceo, SHA-256 tokenHash, allowedJoinTypes=human, expiresAt, invitedByUserId=system, revoked/accepted timestamps}; raw pcp_bootstrap_ token; deployment mode, DB URL and base URL. There is no named deployment owner, company/legal entity, accountable initiating human, scope/audience, one-time transaction ID, MFA requirement or immutable bootstrap audit record.
units.lifecycle: Load env/config -> require authenticated mode -> resolve DB -> count existing admins -> optionally bypass with force -> revoke active unused bootstrap invites -> generate 192-bit token -> clamp requested lifetime to 1 hour-30 days -> insert invite -> derive and print URL -> close DB. Revocation and creation are separate statements without a visible transaction/lock; concurrent commands can race between count/revoke/insert.
units.testAssessment: No focused CLI bootstrapCeoInvite test was found. CLI TypeScript checking passes. The existing completed server bootstrap-claim route assessment was reused without rereading: seven mocked route scenarios cover profile/actor gates, CSRF composition and concurrent-winner conflict, but do not prove this direct DB command, real transactionality, deployment ownership, invite hash timing, brute-force/rate limits, MFA/session freshness, rollback, audit alerts or recovery. Database migration/schema constraints must not be inferred from route mocks.
units.designRationale: An out-of-band local bootstrap path is necessary when no administrator exists. Strong random bearer material, hash-only persistence, human-only join type, bounded lifetime and proactive old-invite revocation are sound primitives. Direct DB access avoids depending on an uninitialized HTTP identity plane but requires much stronger local operator and transaction guarantees.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a secure first-owner ceremony for managed and self-hosted deployments that distinguishes infrastructure operator, instance administrator, company owner and business roles, proves control of the deployment and leaves an accountable immutable record.
units.companyOsFit: Reimplement as a one-time DeploymentClaim capability. Provisioning should create a short-lived, single-use hashed claim bound to deployment ID, canonical origin, intended organization and explicit admin capability; claim acceptance should require a real human identity, fresh authentication/MFA and an atomic compare-and-set. Offline self-hosted recovery may use a console-generated code but must record operator evidence. Business CEO and instance-admin roles must remain distinct.
units.responsibilityConflict: The command equates bootstrap CEO with instance administration and records invitedByUserId=system, leaving no accountable human initiator. --force can create another authority-granting invite even after an admin exists. Company OS cannot let an Agent, generic system actor or database-capable process silently manufacture human administrative authority without a deployment-owner ceremony and evidence chain.

units.securityFindings: Critical privilege bootstrap path: any local actor with command execution and DB credentials can generate an instance-authority invite; --force bypasses the existing-admin guard. Admin count, old-invite revocation and new insert are not one transaction/serialized invariant, so failure after revocation leaves no invite and concurrent runs may create multiple valid invites. Explicit/environment base and DB URLs are not validated here; a malicious base URL can produce a phishing invite and DATABASE_URL can redirect privileged writes. The raw bearer URL is printed to terminal/log capture. SHA-256 storage and 192-bit randomness are positive, but no attempt/rate limit, claim audience/deployment binding, MFA, operator identity or audit event is visible. Invalid NaN expiresHours can escape the intended clamp and fail unpredictably.
